## Summary

Follow-up to #253. That PR's "What Beadle Is" section fixed two
misunderstandings (personal-inbox framing, privileged "owner" role) but
missed the two that actually cost the most correction rounds in the
conversation that produced it:

- **"Is a human watching" isn't a security boundary anywhere in this
  system.** `beadle-email` runs its own poller (`cmd/beadle-email/admin_cmd.go`)
  and can act unattended just as much as `beadle-daemon` can. Nothing in
  the doc said so, which left the door open to rebuilding "daemon =
  autonomous, email = interactive only" — exactly wrong.
- **What actually differs between the two binaries** is what a permission
  grant unlocks: `beadle-email`'s `r`/`w` lets a message become a real
  prompt the agent reasons about; `beadle-daemon`'s `x` only lets it pick
  among pre-signed recipes. That distinction — judgment vs. fixed
  execution — is also the actual reason only recipes need an extra
  authorizer-signature lock, not attendance.

Also adds `docs/artifacts/trust-model-explainer.html` — a self-contained,
plain-language walkthrough of the same model, for someone who won't read
`ARCHITECTURE.md` — and a docs-map entry for it.

## Test plan

Docs-only — Phase 3 verification N/A. `markdownlint-cli2 CLAUDE.md
docs/README.md`: 0 errors. Read-through confirms the new paragraph is
consistent with the rest of the "What Beadle Is" section and doesn't
contradict `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1
